key_insight: A deep learning model on multichannel interictal intracranial EEG can localize epileptogenic zones with performance comparable to published benchmarks and simple electrophysiology baselines.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could support more reliable presurgical localization for drug-resistant epilepsy across different centers and implantation types.
method: Morlet wavelet temporal Transformer to encode interictal EEG patterns
Permutation-equivariant Induced Set Attention Block to model long-range inter-electrode interactions
Leave-one-center-out validation across seven centers to test generalizability
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 50.5 hours of iEEG from 161 patients and 17,012 channels, the model achieved pooled AUROC 0.778 and performed above chance at all held-out centers.
watch_item: Results are based on retrospective data and an EZ definition tied to Engel Class I surgical outcome, so prospective validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Localizing epileptogenic zones using interictal intracranial electroencephalography and deep learning
